citeAs: Guha, E., Marten, R., Keh, S., Raoof, N., Smymis, G., et al. (2025). Data Recipes for Reasoning Models. OpenThoughts Team.
creator: Etash Guha, Ryan Marten, Sedrick Keh, Negin Raoof, Georgios Smymis, Hritik Bansal, Marianna Nezhurina, Jean Mercat, Trung Vu, Zayne Sprague, and others (Stanford University, BespokeLabs.ai, Toyota Research Institute, UC Berkeley, UT Austin, UCLA, JSC, LAION, NYU, UNC Chapel Hill, ASU, Lila Sciences, Cornell Tech, TUM)
description: A 1,000-example sample subset drawn from the OpenThoughts reasoning dataset series. OpenThoughts datasets consist of question-thinking tokens-answer triplets across math, code, and science domains, where reasoning traces are generated by distillation from teacher models (e.g., DeepSeek-R1, QwQ-32B). This sample is associated with the scaling experiments described in the OpenThoughts paper, which investigates SFT data curation for reasoning models.
name: OpenThoughts-1k-sample
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Extensive ablation experiments (1,000+) were conducted to evaluate each pipeline step. Answer filtering experiments showed that no filtering strategy significantly outperformed training on all samples. Decontamination achieved a 99.6% true negative rate (correctly identifying contaminated samples), with only 1.4% of non-contaminated samples incorrectly discarded. Scaling experiments showed consistent performance improvements from 316 to 1M+ examples across math, code, and science benchmarks.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Reasoning traces (thinking tokens) and answers were generated by teacher models (DeepSeek-R1 or QwQ-32B) for each question. The format is question-thinking tokens-answer triplets. For the 1K sample scale, hyperparameters include: learning rate 2e-5, batch size 96, 7 epochs, no packing. Teacher model sampling used temperature=0.7, top_p=1.0, max_new_tokens=32,768.
rai:dataBiases: The paper found that question source quality strongly affects downstream performance, with a 17.2 point gap between strongest and weakest code datasets. Mixing many question sources degrades performance, suggesting quality concentration bias. The dataset focuses on math, code, and science domains only, excluding other reasoning domains. Reasoning traces are generated by specific teacher models (DeepSeek-R1, QwQ-32B), which may introduce biases from those models. The paper notes that CommonCrawl does not contain long reasoning traces similar to those used by current reasoning models.
rai:dataCollection: Questions were sourced from existing datasets and newly generated datasets across math, code, and science domains. Sources include StackExchange CodeGolf, OpenCodeReasoning, NuminaMath, OpenMath-2-Math, StackExchange Physics, and organic chemistry PDFs, among others. Answers (reasoning traces) were generated by distillation from teacher models (primarily DeepSeek-R1 or QwQ-32B). Multiple answers per question (up to 16×) were sampled from the teacher model.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw questions sourced from: StackExchange forums (CodeGolf, Physics, Biology), competitive programming datasets (OpenCodeReasoning, CodeContests), math competition datasets (NuminaMath-1.5, OpenMath-2-Math), organic chemistry PDFs and textbooks, and other online sources. Reasoning traces were generated by teacher models (DeepSeek-R1, QwQ-32B) rather than collected from humans.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web Scraping, Software Collection, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataLimitations: The paper notes: (1) datasets for reinforcement learning were not explored; (2) staged SFT or curriculum learning was not explored; (3) distilled reasoning models show generalization deficits (strong performance fluctuations on reasoning-invariant problem variations); (4) safety alignment is degraded by SFT on reasoning data; (5) the pipeline optimizes for average benchmark performance rather than per-domain optimization; (6) the 1K sample is a small subset used primarily for scaling experiments and may not represent the full dataset quality.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Sampling multiple answers per question (up to 16×) from teacher models to increase dataset scale. Exact deduplication applied to math and science questions; no deduplication for code questions. Questions filtered by LLM-annotated difficulty (GPT-4o-mini) for code, and by response length (GPT-4.1-mini) for math and science. Scaling experiments conducted at dataset sizes from 316 to 31,600 examples (log-scale midpoints).
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Pipeline includes: (1) question sourcing from 27 code, 21 math, and 14 science sources; (2) question mixing (top 1-2 sources per domain); (3) question filtering using LLM-based difficulty scoring (GPT-4o-mini) or response length filtering (GPT-4.1-mini); (4) deduplication using exact match or fuzzy (Indel similarity) deduplication; (5) generating multiple answers per question (16×) from teacher model; (6) decontamination against evaluation benchmarks using Indel similarity (75% threshold) and N-gram similarity (N=13).
rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper notes that supervised fine-tuning on reasoning data inadvertently degrades the pre-existing safety alignment of base models. OpenThinker3-7B (trained on the full dataset) achieved a harmfulness rate of 55.5% on Harmbench, compared to 14.5% for the base Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct model. The dataset was released without explicit safety-tuning or alignment-focused data. The authors acknowledge this trade-off between reasoning capabilities and safety.
rai:dataUseCases: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) of language models to develop reasoning capabilities in math, code, and science domains. Intended for training reasoning models that produce long chains of thought (thinking tokens) during inference. Used to train OpenThinker models. The 1K sample is used in scaling experiments to evaluate data recipe performance at small dataset sizes.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: DeepSeek-R1 (primary teacher model for answer/reasoning trace generation), QwQ-32B (alternative teacher model), GPT-4o-mini (question difficulty scoring, response length filtering, question generation for some sources, verification), GPT-4.1-mini and GPT-4.1-nano (response length filtering), FastText classifiers (question and answer filtering), OpenAI text-embedding-3-large (embedding-based filtering), Gemini gemini-2.0-flash-lite-preview-02-05 (OCR for PDF extraction)

null_reasons.rai:annotationsPerItem: The paper describes generating up to 16 answers per question for the full pipeline, but the 1K sample specifically does not have a stated fixed number of annotations per item.
null_reasons.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotations are generated by AI teacher models (DeepSeek-R1, QwQ-32B), not human annotators, so demographics are not applicable.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: No human annotation platform used; annotations generated programmatically via teacher model APIs (DeepSeek API, etc.).
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: No specific data collection timeframe or date range is mentioned in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: No discussion of missing data handling in the dataset collection process.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation protocol described; the dataset consists of generated question-answer pairs without missing value imputation.
null_reasons.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: No versioning or maintenance plan described beyond releasing artifacts on Hugging Face and GitHub.
null_reasons.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Dataset consists of math, code, and science reasoning problems with no personal or sensitive information.
null_reasons.license: The specific ryanmarten/OpenThoughts-1k-sample dataset has no license listed on HuggingFace, and the paper does not state a license for this specific sample subset.
